<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1063c369a9fa9e06f6179be3cc300bed2a4c495e` — the merge of head `d53f230cdbb30a02fa004b6c325a55778acc71fd` into base `9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1063c369a9fa9e06f6179be3cc300bed2a4c495e && git checkout 1063c369a9fa9e06f6179be3cc300bed2a4c495e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260 d53f230cdbb30a02fa004b6c325a55778acc71fd && git checkout -B drift-repro 9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260 && git merge --no-ff d53f230cdbb30a02fa004b6c325a55778acc71fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9b0de7de73699771b69649bf7b507fbd2a842260` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d53f230cdbb30a02fa004b6c325a55778acc71fd`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #20912 (body and all seven comments — the serial order `5921389276`, the resume `5922687245`, the dev report `5923231598` and the seat's ACCEPT `5923261960` included), PR #21019 (body, its 8-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge base `f8178ffece`), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: the spec predicates, the engine's two doors and the gate scripts were read from the tree at the head; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Surface, against the serial order `5921389276` and the resume `5922687245`.**
- `analytics-service.ts` changes in exactly two hunks (+10 / −3), each a granted call site: `compile()`'s probe handed to `compileDataset` (base line 1887; the key is renamed with the published option) and the lambda handed to `assertNoStructuredJsonDimension` (base line 2790). Each answers `{ type: meta.type, multiple: meta.multiple === true }` behind the same `typeof meta?.type !== 'string' || meta.type === ''` guard the strategy context's `declaredValueShape` builder already uses (head line 1282). The strategy context's own `declaredFieldType` (line 1277) is untouched. **Right** — the order's two call sites, in the shape it named, and nothing else in the file.
- The rest of the diff: the door, the dataset compiler, three new pin files on the claim's surface (`service-analytics/src/__tests__/`, `packages/rest/src/analytics-*.test.ts`), one GUARD re-judged, one changeset. No `packages/objectql/src`, no `packages/spec/src`, no governed path (queue guard green). **Right.**

**No second copy of the rule.**
- Door, grouped members: `groupedClassOf` asks `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`, then `isMultiValueField(shape)` — the engine's `jsonStoredGroupTargets` (`packages/objectql/src/group-by-structured-json-door.ts`): the same two predicates, in the same order. **Right.**
- Door, measures: `distinctClassOf` gates on the `FieldType` vocabulary, then `isAggregateCompatibleWithFieldType('count_distinct', type)` beside `isMultiValueField(shape)` — the engine's `jsonStoredDistinctTargets` (`count-distinct-json-stored-door.ts`), line for line. **Right.**
- Dataset compiler: `flaggedList` holds only for `count_distinct` over a type the table's row accepts while `isMultiValueField` says the declaration is a list; the type row still refuses `tags` alone, with its existing words; the flag row names `with multiple: true`. Only `count_distinct` can be moved by the flag: the `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` rows hold numeric, temporal and boolean types only, none of them in `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` (read in `aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts` at the head). **Right.**
- No field type is listed by name anywhere in the analytics source; every list in the module header and the changeset is prose. Both GUARDs compute the expected verdict from the spec predicates over every `FieldType`, bare and flagged. **Right.**

**Accept-set narrowings the diff publishes** (`@objectstack/service-analytics`; through it `POST /api/v1/analytics/query`, `/analytics/sql` and `/analytics/dataset/query`):
1. A grouped `dimensions` entry, or a bucketed `timeDimensions` entry, whose column is a multi-value field → `INVALID_FIELD` / 400 on both strategies, on the cube and dataset faces and the dry run, naming the member the caller wrote. Before (dev's readings, both dialects): one group per serialized array on SQLite and 500 on PostgreSQL on the native strategy; the engine's `groupBy[0]` words on the ObjectQL strategy. **Right** — the engine door's refusal, plus the card's fold-in.
2. A `measures` entry that resolves to `count_distinct` over a JSON-stored column (the type row, or the declaration) → `INVALID_FIELD` / 400; an authored measure, a suffix-inferred one and a compiled dataset's are one population; `count` is not judged. **Right.**
3. A dataset `count_distinct` over a base-object field declared `multiple: true` → `DATASET_INVALID` / 400 at compile time (registration and the request door), beside the type row that already refused `tags`. A dotted path is left to the door at query time, on the joined object. **Right** — the card's row 3, the declaration half.
Controls unchanged: a scalar dimension, a scalar `count_distinct`, `count` over a multi-value column, a dotted path with no declared join, a host that wires no `sourceFieldMeta`. **Right.**

**Public-surface change.** `DatasetCompileOptions.declaredFieldType` (the type-only probe) is removed and `declaredValueShape` is added, answering `ValueShapeFieldDef | undefined`. `DatasetCompileOptions` is exported from the package index; its only in-repo caller is `analytics-service.ts`. **Right that the change is necessary** (row 3 is undecidable from the type alone) **and right that it is BREAKING** for a host calling `compileDataset` directly — a TypeScript host is told at its own call site; a host passing neither probe compiles exactly as before.

**Words.** Verdict, "The query was NOT run.", route, reason — #20807's member-named form, with "the engine" read as "analytics". One deliberate difference: the multi-value route names a record query on the declaring object with `$contains`, not this service's own `where`, because the native strategy compiles `$contains` over a JSON-stored column to `LIKE` (the dev's measurement: a substring over-count on SQLite, 500 on PostgreSQL; routed by the seat to #20987). **Right**: the engine door's code and structure, and a route that does not send the author into a second defect.

**Pins.** Red first (`f88977bf4e`: 16 / 21, 6 / 10, GUARD 1 / 13, REST 2 red), then the fix (`2c1b093a66`); seven ablation legs, each turning exactly its predicted pins red, and a dist leg for the REST pin. Live-driver cells: SQLite always; PostgreSQL by name-skip without `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, so un-run in CI, as each file header says. **Right** as the dev's evidence; not re-run here.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/20912-analytics-multi-value-distinct-refused.md`: `@objectstack/service-analytics: minor`, headed `fix(service-analytics)!:`, a `**BREAKING**` banner naming the three narrowings and the published rename, and a "Your fix" paragraph in prose (`declaredFieldType` is gone; pass `declaredValueShape`, answering `{ type, multiple }` or `undefined`). **Right.** A breaking narrowing ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` until GA); `patch` would understate a published-surface change (WHICH LEVEL: a `fix(` that changes the public surface does not stay `patch`). `@objectstack/rest` gains only a test, so no second changeset is owed. **Right.**
- BREAKING banner and prose remedy: the banner states what narrows, where it holds, who is affected and what is unchanged; the remedy states FROM → TO and the one-line fix. It is prose, as the landed `20648` changeset's is (its own history: "state the stand-in fix in prose and rest the runtime-interface-only claim on a body with no migration prescription"). **Right.**
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts#DatasetCompileOptions)`: the symbol resolves to an exported interface at the head; its file is not `*.zod.ts`, not under `packages/spec/src/contracts/`, not an object definition; it is not a projection of a Zod schema; no metadata surface names it (`git grep -w` over `*.zod.ts` and `packages/spec/src/contracts/**` at the head: none); the body carries no arrow-form or table-form prescription; the other categories are closed on facts (`type-surface-only` is the real sixth category, #13080, and the interface was concretely typed at the base). `Check Changeset` is green on the head. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, in the PR body and in the changeset. The diff narrows three accept sets and replaces one member of a published options interface. I weighed `yes (narrowing)` — "widens one surface and narrows another" — because `declaredValueShape` is accepted where it was not. I judge **`no (narrowing)` right**: the value answers whether the card loosens an accept set or enlarges the public surface, and a one-for-one member replacement enlarges nothing — the interface has the same three optional members, no new capability is exposed and nothing new can be authored. `yes` is the additive case (WHICH LEVEL: "a new exported symbol on an index, a new accepted key or value"; this package's own `2b53993` added two members and removed none, and reads `yes (widening)`). The repo's precedent for a member move on a published runtime interface is `20648` (`find` → `findOne` on `MigrationFlagEngine` and `SeedTenancyLedger`, deliberately regraded "as a narrowing of two published engine interfaces"), and it reads `no (narrowing)`. Both spellings carry the same consequences — at least `minor`, BREAKING, an ADR-0087 disposition — so no gate reading changes either way; the line as written is the truthful one.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none. Every dev flag and every `out_of_scope_findings` entry:
- NOT MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` → carried by `Build Core` (ci.yml line 2145): **green** on the head. NOT MEASURED `check:type-check-debt` → `Type Check · debt ledger` (lint.yml line 6312): **green**. Answered.
- NOT MEASURED MySQL → the refusals precede any SQL (every pin counts zero raw statements and zero aggregates reaching the engine), so the dialect does not enter the verdict. Answered.
- PostgreSQL cells un-run in CI → the dev's PostgreSQL 16.13 readings, on a server its run started and removed; the pins are red-capable and skip by name. Accepted as the dev's measurement; this seat is read-only and did not re-run them.
- Downstream consumer suites declared to CI → `Test Core` 1–6, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1–3, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`: see the check-run line below.
- The published rename → judged in ②.
- The door and its file not renamed; the two call-site comments still say "declared type" → accepted: a rename would move `analytics-service.ts` past the two granted lambdas, and the module header says what the door judges. Debt for the next touch of that file, not a defect.
- `$contains` over a JSON-stored column compiled to `LIKE` on the native strategy → the seat routed it to #20987 (ACCEPT `5923261960`). Answered.
- The lint rule `measure-aggregate-field-type-refused` judging the type only → routed to #20890. Answered.
- The pinned sibling (AGENTS.md Post-Task #4, a renamed export): `Console Pin Gate` skipped on this head because the `console` filter watches only `.objectui-sha` and the console build scripts; that build bundles this tree's `@objectstack/client` and `@objectstack/spec` into the console, not `@objectstack/service-analytics`, so the console is not a consumer of `DatasetCompileOptions`. A direct grep of objectui at the pin `db11afd4` could not be run from this seat (code search is repository-bound). Not blocking; the owning seat's landing grep remains its own step.
- Docs drift (`5923207417`): six hand-written pages name the literal `count_distinct`; this PR edits no docs, and the changeset carries the user-facing words. Non-blocking; the seat may route a re-verification.

Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-01T02:19Z, all completed: 34 total — 31 `success` (`Test Core` and its six shards, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and its three shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace` / `source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, the four PR-claim guards, `filter`, `Auto Label`), 3 `skipped` by path filter (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, 0 in progress. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts this record rests on.
